story_title: Windows NTLM hash disclosure spoofing CVE-2024-43451 listed in the KEV catalog

provenance.note: Live end-to-end holdout v6 candidate. KEV membership verified against the seeded live CISA catalog feed on 2026-10-10 (Microsoft Windows NTLM Hash Disclosure Spoofing). Keywords are the official product words from the KEV entry and the NVD description (OR semantics; a legitimate insufficient_evidence outcome is scored by unknown_honesty). Disjoint from both development datasets and all consumed holdouts (v1-v5). Independent review: glm-5.3-flash=high:MSRC advisory for CVE-2024-43451 names Windows products and describes an NTLM hash disclosure spoofing vulnerability (Nov 2024 Patch Tuesday), grounding both 'windows' and 'ntlm' row keywords and a 'propose' outcome. NVD corroborates the Windows NTLM Hash Disclosure Spoofing description. CISA has added CVE-2024-43451 to the KEV catalog, so known_exploited=yes is genuinely supported. Allowing both propose and insufficient_evidence is conservative since the advisory does name affected products.; deepseek-v4.1-flash=high:MSRC advisory for CVE-2024-43451 is a Windows NTLM hash-disclosure/spoofing flaw (NTLM named explicitly in the title), and the CVE is genuinely present in the CISA KEV catalog (added 2024-11-12), so known_exploited=yes is correct. row_contains 'windows','ntlm' both appear in the official advisory/NVD description, and the allowed outcome set {propose, insufficient_evidence with preserved unknowns} is consistent with available product/version detail.; kimi-k2.8-preview=high:CVE-2024-43451 is genuinely in the CISA KEV catalog (added 2024-11-12 Patch Tuesday, exploitation detected in the wild), so known_exploited=yes is supported.
